clue.text: Looking offended by power trip

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
an outing is a short trip or excursion

explanation.surface: Someone sulking because a person in charge is on a power trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Pouting means pushing out the lips in a sulky way, the face of someone who feels hurt.

clue.text: Display anti-aircraft gun, ignoring one order

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the order's letters drop from the gun

parts.note: a pom-pom is a rapid-firing anti-aircraft gun
OM is the Order of Merit, one British order

explanation.surface: Showing off an anti-aircraft gun but disobeying a command.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour, abbreviated OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is ceremonial splendour, a grand show put on for spectators.

clue.text: Tongue bends double, finding way in

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the road letters go between the two bends

parts.note: a U-bend is a U-shaped bend, so a bend gives U
double asks for the bend a second time, giving another U
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A tongue bending back on itself to find a way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' is a link word; 'Tongue' means language, not the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language of Pakistan and India, and tongue is a common word for a language.

clue.text: Controlling what one arrested may be given

definitions.text: what one arrested may be given
definitions.meaning: a person arrested is charged, so may be put '...', the old phrase for taken into custody

explanation.surface: What a person under arrest might be handed by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in charge means having authority, and 'given in charge' is the old phrase for handing someone to the police.

clue.text: Dodgy Russian showing a bit of brain

indicators.note: showing means put on view, so the answer is displayed inside the words that follow and precede

explanation.surface: A shifty Russian displaying some intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' signals letters on view within 'Dodgy Russian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyrus is one of the ridges on the surface of the brain's cortex.

clue.text: Purported cure tested her good faith

indicators.note: a thing tested is tried out and put through changes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claimed remedy put someone's sincerity on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tested' signals rearranging HERGOODFAITH, which spells out the twelve letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink taken the morning after to ease a hangover is folk medicine of doubtful worth, hence only a supposed remedy.

clue.text: Metal prostheses set these off?

parts.note: AL is the chemical symbol for aluminium, a metal
artificial arms are prostheses

explanation.surface: Wondering whether metal artificial limbs trigger security scanners.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: metal arms would set off airport alarms.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarms are warning devices triggered by detectors, as at airport security when metal passes through.

clue.text: In which one can winningly play to the gallery

definitions.text: In which one can winningly play to the gallery

parts.words: In which one can winningly play to the gallery
parts.note: in the indoor court game, striking the ball into the opening called the winning gallery wins the point; 'play to the gallery' normally means showing off to the crowd

explanation.surface: A sport where showing off to the audience pays.
explanation.definitionFit: Real tennis, the original indoor racket game, has openings called galleries, one of them a target that wins a point outright.

clue.text: Left tights off for check-up

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone stripping off their tights for a medical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals rearranging LEFTTIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight test is a check on an aircraft or pilot carried out in the air.

clue.text: Millions are putting in short order for arrangement of treatment

indicators.note: the pair M and ARE take something placed between them, so this phrase signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: A command about millions of pounds being spent on organising health care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the order word, and 'putting in' places what is left between M and ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicare is the name of a public health insurance scheme, a system set up to fund medical care.

clue.text: Is no longer a swinger? That's pungent

parts.note: was is the past tense of is, describing what no longer holds
BI is short for bisexual, someone who swings both ways

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person has given up swinging, and finds the idea distasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinger' plays on the slang 'swings both ways' for a bisexual person.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is the fiery green Japanese condiment, a paste with a sharp, nose-tingling heat.

clue.text: Hard villains finally cheated in hearing

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word villains
in hearing means as heard spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: tricked means cheated

explanation.surface: Tough criminals in the end swindled at their trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict means severe or rigorous, as a hard taskmaster is.

clue.text: About to rest, change striker for amateur game

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for change goes round the word for rest

parts.note: to vary is to change
to sit is to rest
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A coach about to bench a forward and swap in someone else for a friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer but is a matchstick. The annual Oxford–Cambridge contests are the varsity matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A varsity match is a game between university teams, especially Oxford and Cambridge, played by students rather than professionals.

clue.text: Bored, virtually carry out an unruly youth

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to perform is to carry out
an is the indefinite article, A
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a rebellious 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: A tearaway youngster, close to performing, is bored stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' means drilled through, not weary. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforated means pierced with holes, the sense of bored as drilled.

clue.text: Get school to raise girl's death

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive, a British state secondary school

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means lifting from bottom to top, so the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: her refers to a girl
an end is a death

explanation.surface: A school's role in bringing up a girl until her death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' means understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to grasp it, the same as comprehending it.

clue.text: All you need to know about love: it's devastating and is huge

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the letter for love
devastating means wrecking, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A wry summing-up of romance: overwhelming and enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastating' scrambles ANDISHUGE, and that rearrangement goes 'about' O to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to cut a discussion short because nothing more needs to be explained.

clue.text: Look meaningfully round very fast

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the look word goes about the very letter

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly

explanation.surface: Someone casting a pointed look around and moving very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' means go without food, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food, and to starve is to suffer from lack of it.

clue.text: Fool that a pedant picks

definitions.meaning: a silly person, as in nitwit
a ... is a louse egg, and a pedant 'picks ...', finding fault over trivial details

explanation.surface: A fool is the sort of thing a fussy critic singles out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nit means a dimwit in British slang, and nitpicking is petty fault-finding.

clue.text: Perhaps good in a sport, showing skill

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the good letter goes inside the sport

parts.note: RU is rugby union
ably means skilfully

explanation.surface: Maybe someone is good at a game, displaying talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Arguably means as can be argued, a tentative maybe.

clue.text: Back page of The Dandy

indicators.note: back means read from the end, so the words page and of run in reverse

explanation.surface: The last page of the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy was a long-running British comic, making 'The Dandy' look like a title rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is a man overly concerned with his clothes and appearance, just what a dandy is.

clue.text: Cutting some potatoes set out in cold winds

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the rearranged letters go inside the potato word

parts.note: earlies are early potatoes, the first crop of the season

indicators.note: out means disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: chop up some potatoes laid out against the chilly wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Earlies are the first new potatoes of the season; 'out' scrambles the word set and 'Cutting' drives it into them.
explanation.definitionFit: Easterlies are winds blowing from the east, which in Britain bring cold continental air.

clue.text: Expecting data, not quite everything

parts.note: info is information, data

indicators.note: not quite means falling short by the last letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Waiting for information that is not entirely complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' means pregnant, of a mare.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare carrying a foal is pregnant, the sense of expecting as in expecting a baby.

clue.text: Endless capital employed by minister a bonus as betting is over

indicators.note: something employed by another is taken inside it, so the trimmed city goes within the minister

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a minister of religion

indicators.note: endless means losing both its first and last letters

parts.note: Vienna is the capital of Austria
a plus is an advantage or bonus

explanation.surface: A city's money handed to a government minister as a bonus once a wager is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' strips VIENNA to IENN, which is 'employed by' REV to make RIENNEV.
explanation.definitionFit: Rien ne va plus is the French croupier's call at roulette closing the table to further bets.

clue.text: Mountains of nettles picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: to pique is to irritate or nettle

explanation.surface: Mountains where nettles have been gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nettles' is a verb (irritates), not the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaks are the pointed tops of mountains, standing for the mountains themselves.

clue.text: Pity it only has 4 chapters

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for pity, as in ruthless
the Book of ... in the Old Testament has four chapters

explanation.surface: A shame that the book is so short.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth means compassion, surviving in ruthless, and the Book of Ruth is a short biblical book.

clue.text: Flimsy item falling short

indicators.note: falling short means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: a thing is an item

explanation.surface: A flimsy article that is not long enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin material is flimsy, lacking substance or strength.

clue.text: See 5
Architect's trade vehicle, brown and horrible

parts.note: a van is a tradesman's vehicle
BR is an abbreviation for brown
ugh is an exclamation at something horrible

explanation.surface: An architect's work van, brown and ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Vanbrugh was the English Baroque designer of Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard.

clue.text: Comedian takes extremely large piece of cake

parts.note: Ken Dodd was a famous British comedian

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the outermost letters, of the next word

explanation.surface: A comedian helps himself to a huge slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a long-serving Liverpool comic known for his tickling stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A doddle is British slang for something very easy, as a piece of cake is idiomatically.

clue.text: Cut layer, about a yard — how much do you want?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cut-and-layer pair goes round the yard letter

parts.note: saw is the past tense of cut with a saw, or to cut
Y is the abbreviation for a yard
a hen is a bird that lays eggs

explanation.surface: A tailor trimming a layer of cloth to around a yard asks how much is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' is read as one that lays: a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Say when is what a host says while pouring, asking the guest to signal the desired quantity.
